extracted.intended_audience: European patent applicants, patent attorneys, and EPO examiners/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the content, wording and purpose of patent claims under Article 84 EPC and related Implementing Rules and case law, to ensure claims properly define the protected subject-matter and enable determination of the extent of protection. Useful for drafting claims and for EPO examination/appeal assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define the matter for which protection is sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 84 EPC provides that claims must define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational purpose of claims: they set out the subject-matter to be protected. The wording of the claim must therefore allow the protection sought to be identified. See R.43 EPC for form and content of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should be clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be clear and concise and be supported by the description (Art. 84 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and conciseness are required to ensure that the scope of protection can be determined. The boards of appeal repeatedly emphasise clarity for legal certainty (e.g. T 337/95; T 586/97; T 437/98; T 728/98; T 1074/00; T 560/09; T 754/13; T 129/13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description (Art. 84 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support by the description ensures that the claims are not broader than the disclosure and that the invention as claimed is grounded in the application. This requirement is assessed in light of the description and the skilled person's understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording must satisfy Art.84 and Implementing Rule requirements considering invention's nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary aim of the wording used in a claim must be to satisfy the requirements under Art. 84 and R.29(1) EPC 1973 (R.43(1) EPC), having regard to the particular nature of the invention, and the purpose of the claims (G 2/88).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim drafting must be tailored to the invention and the claims' purpose; literal/formal phrasing alone is not sufficient if it fails to meet Art.84/R.43 criteria. Consider both legal/formal requirements and the technical character of the invention when choosing wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must enable the protection conferred to be determined (extent of protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of claims under the EPC is to enable the protection conferred by the patent or patent application to be determined (Art. 69 EPC), and thus the rights of the patent owner within the designated contracting states (Art. 64 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be drafted so third parties, courts and authorities can ascertain the extent of protection; the claim's wording determines scope and thus the rights conferred across contracting states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be considered with regard to patentability requirements (Arts. 52–57 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of claims must be considered having regard to the patentability requirements of Art. 52 to 57 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Art.84 is a formal/content requirement, claims cannot be divorced from substantive patentability considerations: what is claimed must be coherent with novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, etc., when assessing scope and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must provide legal certainty / public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear for the sake of legal certainty; the public should not be left in any doubt as to which subject-matter is covered and which is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal certainty is paramount where a monopoly affects public rights (see T 81/14). Claims serve as public notice; ambiguous claims undermine legal certainty and are objectionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must allow the skilled person to establish demarcation of scope without undue burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The skilled person should be able to establish the demarcation of the scope of the claim (i.e. its extent of protection) without undue burden (T 754/13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a person skilled in the art can, using the claim as drafted (and the description if necessary), determine whether a particular embodiment falls within the claim, without excessive analysis or interpretation.
